x: Charlie Walker again refused to cane himself over the last mile and was content with 4th. Following him were Tooby, Bedford, Burr, Trower, Brickwood, L. Bishop and Newell making one of his too infrequent appearances.
Cliff Roffey came through for second, Short 3rd., Walker 5th and then the pack Bagnall, Gebbett, Burr, Brickwood and Trower 7th to 11th to make sure of the team race.

The going did not suit Colin Collis at all and Burr and Bishop had obviously not fully recovered from colds. Jim Masters unfortunately injured his foot again on the iron hard ground; he had already done so once this season in the Inter Counties.
Burr gained a place but Bagnall was passed by Ken Norris, T.V.H. who did 17.42, the fastest time of the day. Walker gained two places and Roffey put us in the lead.

Bedford and Walker then made sure of our victory though Charlie took things a little too easy in the middle and so we missed the course record by one second. Burr ran well on the last leg for the "B" team whilst Rolls, Whitehead and Herbert brought the Vets safely home for their prizes.

However he maintained our position and sent off Jon Burr, still sixth. Jon ran above his recent form (for which we were grateful) and set about catching T.V.H. and H.H.H. which, to the great delight of our supporters in coaches, did so just as we were passing him.

S.L.H. opened with Ashworth and a new course record, Burr running quite well for 4th place. Peter Bagnall was passed by Sando who also put up a new course record, but Jon also passed two himself and finished 3rd.
